Emrakul, the Exigent Doom: Trap — don't take it. 51.9% with +0.1 IWD, and the 47.7% opening-hand WR shows it rotting in hand exactly as Numot and LR (F) predicted. Ward is paid with three lands late, the colorless ramp costs a card, and even R/G ramp has better top end in Crusher and Kiora.
Academic Ascent: Filler trick, 23rd card at best. 52.6% sits well under the 55.1% mean; Empower 2 is two surveils, not a card. Only W/U (+1.0) gets anything from it. In R/W (-2.6) it is a liability. The C- grades were right and DS's optimism was not.
Blossom-Blessed Angel: Solid playable that beats its DS 1.5 and C grades: LoL's read was right. A 4-mana flier that becomes a 3/5 or stacks a counter guards your Jace and pecks over a stalled board. 55.9% with +2.5 IWD; strongest in WB and WU (+2.8/+2.7). Take it over most white filler.
Campus Crier: Solid playable two-drop: 55.7% GIH, right at the mean, and the 56.9% OH says it earns its slot early by pressuring Jace tokens. Neutral in W/U (+0.4), slightly negative in W/R and G/W, so it's a curve-filler, not a pick to chase. Save the graveyard empower for after your Jace dies.
Enlightened Confidant: Premium two-drop, better than the C+ grades: 58.0% with a 60.9% opening-hand WR, so it's a real early play that keeps paying off, not a late-game card. Lifelink turns on its own surveil every attack. Best in G/W (+5.4) with repeatable gain; fine but ordinary in W/U (+2.0).
Fateshaper Aspirant: Filler-minus 23rd card. A 5-mana 3/4 with a small ETB is exactly the cheap body this slow format punishes; 51.9% with negative IWD in W/B, G/W and R/W confirms LLU's "definition of filler." Only W/U (+1.3) tolerates one copy, and only when you have a legend worth rebuying.
Flickering Hound: Trap. 45.2% GIH and -5.3 IWD make it one of the worst-performing rares: a 4-mana 2/2 that does nothing on arrival dies to the format's sweepers and blockers before the blink engine starts. The experts' D grades were right and the 'dreamer' upside almost never shows up. Leave it in the sideboard.
Generous Revival: Solid playable that beats its C-/C+ grades: 57.2% with positive IWD in every white pair (best W/U +3.3, G/W +3.0), not just the W/B grind home LLU named. In a slow format, two reanimations of an ETB three-drop are a real two-for-one. One copy is right; a second wants good targets.
Germinate Recruits: Trap. 47.7% with -2.3 IWD confirms the experts: this set gains life one point at a time, so X is usually 0-1 and the card is a blank. Even G/W lifegain can't assemble it reliably; only a Vigorbloom Charm dream deck should touch it.
Graft Surgeon: Filler or worse. At 51.5% it is negative in every white pair, worst in W/B (-2.0), and is not even a plus in G/W counters (-0.6). A vanilla 3/3 for 3 has no lasting impact in this slow format, and exile or lockdown removal strands the counter. LR 874 says avoid it; take it pick 10+ at best.
Guiding Hydra: Premium rare, first-pick quality: 57.3% GIH with +4.6 IWD and positive in every white pair, best in W/B (+5.1) and W/U (+4.8). It plays as a big body that pumps the team every combat; R/W (+3.3) is its weakest home despite going wide. Splashable, but kill it before combat if you face it.
Hexhaven Battalion: Premium white common; take it over Unflinching Hortimancer and most non-removal. A cycle-on-turn-2 land early and three bodies plus a Jace draw late is what this slow format pays for. Best in U/B splash or W/U (+7.7, +3.6); still positive in every white pair.
Kindred Judgment: Bomb rare, and LR's 874 upgrade was right: 61.4% with +8.0 IWD makes it a top-tier white card in a slow, stall-prone format. Best in W/U (+9.1) and G/W (+6.8); weak in W/B (+1.7), which already has spot removal. Name your best tribe or nothing. Double-pip splashable in slow decks.
Loyal Tutor: Don't play it (provisional, no live WR, 2.5% play rate). Putting a walker on top costs a full card and a turn's draw. In a slow format that wants card advantage, that's a pure loss. LR F and Numot agree. LLU's D only applies with two real bomb walkers, and even then skip it.
Memory Trap: Good removal: a 3-mana O-Ring that answers bombs, Ways and Jace tokens alike. 55.8% overall, but it peaks in UB (+4.5) and WU (+2.4) and goes flat in WB/WR (-0.4/-0.8), where it is mainly a body-light answer. Early pick in blue, solid elsewhere.
Predictive Preparations: Trap. 48.5% GIH is the lowest white common, and IWD is negative in every pair, worst in W/B (-7.7) and W/R (-5.2). A slow format rewards removal and card draw, not counters on bodies that get stalled. LR's post-release 'missed really hard' settles the Numot split; leave it in the sideboard.
Prophesied End: Premium removal even though its 55.1% sits at the set mean. The low opening-hand WR comes from slow boards where the opponent draws off it; held for an attacker or a must-kill, it's a two-mana Murder. Strongest in W/B (+3.7) and W/U (+3.1); flat in G/W.
Refute Destiny: Sideboard card, as all three guides say. 53.3% hides a decent W/U number (+3.1 IWD) because it gets boarded in against the blue and green decks it kills; in Bo1, maindeck it only if you've seen the opponent's colours lean U/G.
Repurposed Enforcer: Premium two-drop, close to first-pick. 59.8% GIH and +7.1 IWD, with a 63.2% opening-hand WR that marks it as a card you want early. It's the rare cheap body that lasts, because every attack threatens a big Jace. Best in R/W (+9.2), which badly needs it, and strong in W/U (+7.4). Grades well below 3 badly undersold it.
Return to the Light Realms: Trap. 50.0% GIH and a 44.9% opening-hand WR confirm the experts' F: nine mana is turn 15, and it does nothing if your graveyard is thin. Even in this slow format, leave it in the sideboard.
Shatterwing Pegasus: Filler. A 3-mana 2/3 flier blocks fine in a stall-heavy format, but 53.5% and flat-to-negative IWD everywhere (-1.8 in R/W, the go-wide deck it supposedly pays off) show the 5-mana pump rarely matters. Take it only as a 23rd card in W/U.
Surgical Precision: Premium common removal. Take it over most white commons. At 57.3% with +3.5 IWD, a third of the set's creatures have toughness 4+, and the draw-a-card mode means it is never dead. Best in W/U (+4.5), positive in every white pair. Numot and Alex B- were right; LR's sorcery-speed C undersold it.
Unflinching Hortimancer: Filler unless you are G/W: 53.8% GIH, +0.3 IWD, and only G/W (+0.7) is positive; it loses in W/U (-1.0) and R/W (-2.2). LR's 874 sealed note says leave it out. A late pick for Vigorbloom decks with repeatable lifegain, never a priority.
Your Fate Ends Here: Premium removal at instant speed. The MV 3+ floor almost never matters because 2-drops aren't what beats you here. Best in W/U (+4.4), where the surveil helps; roughly neutral in W/B (-0.4), which already has black removal. Play every copy.
Countersculpt: Premium removal-equivalent and a top uncommon (59.6%, +6.0). LLU's B and LoL's 'nuts' beat LR's pre-release C. Wins most in U/B (+7.7) and G/U (+7.2), where you'll often have a Jace to behold. Even a Cancel plus empower is great here, because slow games are decided by expensive threats.
Cruel Calculations: Trap; skip it. 50.0% GIH is near the bottom of the set because it usually draws zero or one card. It needs a self-mill spell cast the same turn, which U/B's Omit Variables does only rarely. LR F / Numot unplayable win out over DS's Theorix optimism.
Cryotheory Adept: Filler you should avoid. A prowess 2/1 falls off fast in a slow format, and the late stun is too little. 53.2% with -0.3 IWD, negative in UR and WU (-1.1/-1.4). LR is right that playing it means your lane was closed. Last-slot only, best in UB (+0.8).
Diviner of Victory: Premium rare that plays well above its C/C+ grades: 59.6% GIH, +6.1 IWD. The prepared bounce reads as tempo but acts as cheap removal against tokens and three-drops. Best in G/U (+8.2) and W/U (+6.3); every blue pair is +5.5 or better. Take it early in any blue deck.
Divining Duelist: Solid blue filler that plays above its 1.5 grade. Flash plus a tap or loot always does something, and it overperforms in the value pairs U/B (+3.7) and G/U (+3.3). It's a weak pick in W/U fliers (+0.6), where it just fills the curve. Usually goes 7th, so wait on it.
Icy Reception: Premium blue removal; take it early. At 57.7% (#5 common) it outruns its C+ grades because it counters creatures, legends, Ways and walkers in a format full of them. Best in U/B (+5.5) and G/U (+4.0); weakest in W/U, where you'd rather tap out for fliers.
Infinite Coursework: Solid playable removal for blue. 55.8% GIH, +2.8 IWD. It shuts off abilities and prepared spells, so it plays above Ben's 'so bad'; LoL's newer C is the fair read. It does most in G/U (+4.6), which has the least removal in the format, and in U/B (+3.4). Untap tricks and bounce can free the creature, but it stays a blank.
Jace's Machinations: Premium card advantage that beats LLU's C+: 57.7% and +5.1 IWD. It plays as an instant two-card draw that leaves a Jace behind. It shines in the Jace-heavy pairs (G/U +7.6, U/B +7.4) and is only modest in W/U and U/R. Take it early in blue.
Mindseeker Oculus: Premium common, the best in the set at 59.8%. It's a 2/1 that draws a card and leaves a Jace token, so it never plays badly. It's +7 in U/B and U/G and positive in every blue pair. LR and LoL both take it over strong uncommons P1P1. Play as many as you find.
Perfected Theory: Filler trick, last-cut territory. 52.0% backs LR and Mark D+ over Alex's 'pushed' read. The 1/1 mode only kills with a block or ping. Only W/U (+2.9) gets real value from it, as a combat-trick blowout in flier races. Elsewhere it is a 23rd card at best.
Plan for All Outcomes: Premium blue removal that plays far above its pre-data C+/B grades: 59.0% GIH, +5.3 IWD. It is a clean tuck plus a steady Jace engine, best in G/U (+7.6) and U/B (+6.3). Take it over most blue commons and uncommons; sorcery speed barely matters in this slow format.
Precise Redaction: Sideboard only. Barely played and too few games for a WR, so this read is provisional; every guide agrees. Hard counters are strong in this format, so bring it in Bo3 against W or B decks. Never maindeck it in Bo1.
Protege's Awakening: Premium common card draw: 58.4%, +5.4 IWD, LR's 874 upgrade confirms it. At worst it's a slow draw-two plus a 3-loyalty Jace that soaks attacks, often a 3-for-1. Strongest in U/B (+6.4) and G/U (+4.6); positive in every blue pair. Take it over most blue creatures, but play one or two copies.
Seasoned Cryomancer: Premium first-pick tier in any blue deck: 58.9%, +6.0 IWD, ALSA 1.7. Double loot plus stuns is a tempo swing and card selection in one, and the graveyard draw-2 punishes late games. Strongest in W/U (+6.3) and U/R (+5.1). Mark's A- beats Alex's B+.
Semester Foreseer: Role-player. A 4-mana 3/4 with surveil plus a 2/2 Cadet is two bodies, but clunky, and the 50.5% OH shows it is slow. 53.7% overall; it overperforms in UG (+3.4) and UB (+2.0) and adds nothing in WU (0.0). Mid-pack filler for UG/UB.
Sphinx of False Conclusions: Bomb: 63.7% GIH, +10.5 IWD. A flash flier that loots and comes back once is a two-for-one that dominates stalled boards. It's huge in U/B (+13.0) and U/R (+10.2), and still +8.6 or more in every blue pair. LLU's 'best rare in the set' holds up. Slam it.
Sphinx's Approach: Good card draw that goes very late (ALSA 7.4): 56.0% in a format won by card advantage, so LLU's D grade was wrong. Ignore the Sphinx clause and play it as an instant Divination in U/B (+3.9) or G/U (+3.0). Skip it in W/U (+0.8), where tempo matters more than cards.
Surveillance Phantasm: Strong playable, roughly a 5th pick, far above its 1.0 DS grade. The vigilant 2/3 flier walls aggro, guards Jace and attacks off its own surveil, and it is positive in every blue pair. Peaks in G/U (+4.3) and U/B (+3.3); merely fine in U/R (+0.8).
The Theorist, Jace Beleren: Bomb. Slam it. 68.4% GIH and +17.4 IWD put it among the very best cards in FRA. In a slow, grindy format, a free card every turn plus a self-protecting +1 is game over. It's strongest in U/B (+19.3) but is +16 or more in every blue pair. Take it over anything except Ajani.
Theorist's Proxy: Solid blue playable at 57.0%: a flash 0/3 that blocks a two-drop and draws a card off the Jace −3, which fits the slow, card-draw format. Best in U/B (+3.0), G/U and W/U; nearly flat in U/R (+0.6), where you want proactive cards. The uncounterable mode rarely matters.
Undulating Witness: Solid playable. The landcycling floor carries it: 55.7% with +2.0 IWD, best in U/G (+3.4) and U/B (+2.9) where splashes and long games reward it. A 3/5 flier is a real stall-breaker when cast. It beats the pre-release C-/D+ grades; never cut it from blue.
Unsummon: Real removal here, and it goes late (ALSA 5.2). At 57.3% it is a premium blue common. It cleanly answers 4/4 and 5/5 Beast tokens, the opponent's Jace token setups and prepared creatures, and leaves mana up next to big draw spells. Best in G/U (+4.6) and U/B (+4.5). LR 876 and LLU agree: the best Unsummon has ever been.
Variable Chaser: Strong playable, better than its C+/2.0 grades: 57.5% GIH, +4.6 IWD. A 2/3 flier for 3 is real value in a stalled format; the wheel is a bonus, not the reason to play it. Best in W/U fliers (+5.3), fine in every blue pair.
Apex Witchstalker: Solid playable and a good landcycler, pick 5th-8th. It's a notch below Hexhaven Battalion, as LR predicted (55.4 vs 57.4). Best in U/B (+2.7) and as a Rewrite Regrets target; it loses in W/B (-2.5) and B/R (-1.5), where aggro bodies want the slot.
Bloodline Recollector: Filler two-drop despite the mythic tag: 51.7%, -0.6 IWD. Three deaths in one turn rarely happens outside sweeper turns, so it's usually a Bear that can't pressure Jace tokens. LR/LLU's C beats Numot's optimism. Only U/B is roughly neutral (+0.2). Take late; don't build around it.
Break Under Pressure: Premium removal and the best black uncommon to take early: 59.6%, +6.5 IWD. Three-mana instant edicts hit their biggest threat in a format full of 4+ toughness bodies. It peaks in U/B (+9.3) and barely helps B/R (+1.5). Alex's 'too low' was right; this is B+ or better.
Cast Away Doubt: UB-only card draw. Overall 53.0% reads like filler, but +4.3 IWD in UB makes it a real 23rd card there, and it falls flat in BR/BG (-0.6/-0.7). LR's guess that it belongs in BR was backwards: take it late for UB control and skip it elsewhere.
Dark Matter Manipulator: Solid playable that beats Numot's 'seems bad': 57.2% GIH, +3.4 IWD. Milling 3 fuels threshold and recursion, and the body grows to 3/2 or 5/2 later. Best in U/B (+4.5) and B/G (+3.5), weakest in B/R (+2.3). Pick it up mid-pack for graveyard decks.
Darklight Phoenix: Overrated mythic: 53.4% is filler despite a 2.4 ALSA. The recursion rarely triggers because combat deaths don't count, so it mostly plays as a four-mana 3/2 flying haste. Only U/B (+2.2) gets value from it, using Silence the Echo and cheap removal. Don't take it over real removal.
Extended Absence: Premium removal and the second-best common (59.2%, +6.2 IWD). Instant-speed exile for any creature or walker is what this removal-hungry format pays for. It's +8.6 in U/B and +6.6 in U/R and G/U; G/W (-0.2) is the only pair where it doesn't lift the deck. Take it over most uncommons.
Extrapolate the Impossible: Unplayable. It sees play in only 4.2% of decks and posts a 47.1% GIH. In Limited it's a 2-mana sorcery where your opponent picks the weaker of two sideboard cards for you, often just a basic land. LR's F and LLU's F/D- were right. The black common landcycler does the fixing job better.
Last Gasp: Premium cheap removal: 56.8%, and one of the few 2-mana instants that kills (−3/−3 handles 68% of creatures). It is a U/B staple (+5.8) and only marginal in B/R and W/B (around 0), which matches black playing best as a control colour. Take it highly in blue-black.
Lich's Relic: Bomb removal; take it over almost anything. 62.4% with +9.7 IWD, +8.5 to +10.6 in every black pair, is targeted kill-anything for 3 that leaves a relevant equipment. It's splashable at one pip, and all experts agree (A-). It's a Rescue Girl rebuy target too.
Multiply by Zero: Premium removal. Take it over almost any uncommon. A 2-mana instant kill on anything without counters plays at 58.9% with +5.9 IWD. Huge in U/B (+8.3) and strong in W/B (+4.2). Weakest in B/R (+2.2) but still a lock there. Every expert called it amazing, and the data agrees.
Overwrite the Multiverse: Bomb, slam it: 65.5% GIH and +13.7 IWD, among the best numbers in the set. A one-sided-in-practice Sunfall that leaves a huge Jace token on the stalled boards this format creates. Peaks in U/B (+15.4) and B/G (+13.9); worth a splash in any black-adjacent control deck.
Rampart Hunter: Trap. A 47.8% GIH WR and 8.6% play rate confirm the D grades. The deathtouch trick does nothing in a format of stalled boards and two-for-ones, and it's negative in B/R and B/G. Take it as the 23rd card only if you have nothing else.
Rank Rat: Role-player that works only in U/B: +3.3 IWD there, flat or negative in W/B, B/G and B/R. Its 55.0% is set average, and discard is weak in a format full of card draw (LLU). The 1/1 body adds nothing outside the control shell, so take it mid-pack for U/B and skip it in aggressive black decks.
Rewrite Regrets: Premium; the biggest grade-vs-data gap in black. 59.3% / +6.3 IWD against C/C+ pre-release grades. LR 874 now calls it a premium zombify. MV 6 still reaches landcyclers, walkers and Vraska, and Empower 2 adds value. Best in U/B (+7.1) and B/G (+5.0). Take it over most commons.
Rise of the Deathbringer: Premium in UB, risky in WB. An instant -3/-3 sweep that punishes the go-wide boards this format builds, or a draw-X when ahead. 55.6% with +3.3 IWD, peaking in UB (+4.9) and BG (+2.7) but -3.4 in WB, where it kills your own white bodies. Early pick for UB control.
Sanctum Lurker: Bomb-tier and far above its 2.5 DS grade: 61.7% GIH, +9.7 IWD. Turn-3 Lurker, +2 to drain, then −3 to draw, and Jace stays at 0 loyalty, so it's a 2-for-1 even after it dies. Over +10 in U/B, B/R and W/B. LR 874 calls it a must-kill and would take it over Liliana. Take it first.
Screeching Soulbreaker: Role-player at 53.5%. A 1/4 flier holds the ground in a stalled format and turns on lifegain, but its drain is too small to win races. Best in U/B (+3.4) as a defensive blocker; flat in B/R (+0.2), so Alex's 'BR pillar' read is wrong. A mid-pack pick.
Silence the Echo: U/B-only removal. With no 1/1 tokens below rare it's usually a 5-mana sorcery kill, so 52.7% overall. In U/B (+3.8) you sacrifice spent Jace tokens for free and it's good; in W/B (-3.2) and B/R (-3.7) it's a trap. Play one copy, never two.
Solve for Disappointment: Filler, U/B only. 52.7% GIH with flat opening-hand and drawn WRs means it's a below-average card all game. It's +2.6 in U/B, where discard-plus-Jace attrition is the plan, and -3.1 in B/R. LR's D- and LLU's C- beat Numot's optimism. A 23rd card at best.
Terminal Criticism: Sideboard card, as all the experts said: 52.3% with a 5.7% play rate. Main-deck play inflates the +3.3 IWD because it only gets played when blue or red decks are expected. Bring it in against U/x or R/x in Bo3. It also kills an opposing Jace token, but not reliably enough to main-deck.
Theoretical Necromancer: Role-player that is better than it reads. The 4/1 trades with 4/4 Beasts, and the real value is milling it for the rebuy. Hence 55.2% GIH with 0.0 IWD: drawing it adds little. It's +1.0 in U/B self-mill and negative in B/R (-3.0); play 2-3 in U/B and skip it elsewhere.
Void Extrapolator: U/B-only filler. It is +2.4 in U/B, where Omit Variables and threshold make the 2-drop body plus mill 3 worthwhile, but negative in B/G, B/R and especially W/B (-2.9). The 55.5% overall comes from U/B decks. LoL's 'actively harmful outside threshold' is confirmed. Pick it mid-pack only when you are U/B.
Vraska's Final Mercy: Solid removal that underperforms its text: 54.4% GIH, +2.1 IWD, low 51.4% OH. The BB cost and life loss hurt outside dedicated black; it shines in U/B (+4.2) but loses in B/R (-2.1). Still take it for U/B, rate it below Prophesied End.
Ajani's Anguish: A good rare but not a slam. The data agrees with LSV over Marshall: 56.2% is only slightly above the mean, and a 51.4% OH WR says it's a late flexible finisher, not tempo removal. Best in B/R (+3.5) and U/R (+3.2), where reach and burn fit. Splashable.
Artifist Acumen: Sideboard card. 49.2%, -2.7 IWD, 9.5% play rate, and negative even in the U/R (-3.3) and B/R (-2.9) prowess decks it was built for. LR (874): 'fallen off a cliff.' Prowess underperforms and team first strike rarely matters when boards stall. Don't take it.
Awaken the Inferno: Solid playable and a near-auto-include: 55.9%. It kills almost anything late, and turn-2 landcycling keeps it from rotting in hand. Best in blue-red builds (U/R +2.7) and splashes (U/G +2.7). It's flat in R/G and B/G, where you want proactive cards. Ranks below the white and black cyclers.
Blazing Crescendo: Trap. A combat trick with card flow, but tricks don't fit this format (LR 874: D-level). 51.8% with a 16% play rate. Only RG gets value (+2.1), and WR is -1.3. Leave it in the pack unless you are low-curve RG and short on playables.
Chandra's Emberling: Filler you play only when short on cards. 51.8% GIH; a 3-mana 2/2 dies to removal before it grows, and prowess-style payoffs underperform here. Only U/R (+1.6) gets anything from it, while W/R (-4.1) and B/R (-2.5) are worse with it. 23rd card at best.
Command the Stage: Trap: 49.8%, negative in every pair, and the worst in R/W (−5.5). LLU calls it the set's biggest disappointment and LR agrees. A 2/2 for three is a bad rate, and noncombat-damage recursion rarely happens below rare. Don't build around it; leave it in the pack.
Craterclaw Colossus: R/G build-around that overperforms: 60.3% when drawn and +8.1 IWD in R/G, against LR's D. The 7 mana is castable in this slow format, and one Heartwood token turns the haste ETB into a finisher. The low 51.5% OH WR means play only one, and only in ramp decks.
Curse-Marred Demon: Solid-to-strong playable, not a bomb. 56.2% GIH and +2.9 IWD: a 4-mana 4/4 flying trampler holds up even in a stalled format, and the Gamble ETB is a wash. Best in R/W (+4.5) and U/R (+3.8), where an evasive finisher closes stalled games. The experts' B/B+ grades are about right. Take it over most commons.
Draconic Visitor: Overrated: 53.1% despite the 4.5 DS grade. A vanilla 5/5 flier for 5 plays below median in this removal-heavy format. It belongs in R/G Heartwood (+4.6), where tokens become dragons, and is negative in U/R and B/R. Take it for R/G, not as a generic red bomb.
Eardrum Rattler: Trap. 49.3% with -4.5 IWD, negative in every red pair (-6.3 in R/G), confirms LLU: the 1-mana activation is too slow and a 2/2 with no lasting impact falls off in this slow format. Pressuring Jace tokens doesn't save it. Sideboard.
Essence Burn: Sideboard only. The 48.8% with a 3.3% play rate shows main-deck copies lose. It is a colour hoser: 5 damage that exiles is excellent against a black or green bomb, so bring it in for Bo3 when the opponent is B/G or a Garruk deck. Never maindeck it in Bo1.
Face Yourself: Situational top-end, better than LR's D: 54.9% GIH, +3.1 IWD. It works only with a planeswalker to keep the copies, so it lives in U/R (+6.5), where Jace tokens and spells line up, and loses in B/R (-2.7). A late one-of for blue Jace decks; skip it elsewhere.
Fulminous Forte: Premium red removal. Five instant damage kills nearly everything, and the 1-damage sweep wipes Jace tokens and 2/2 Cadets. Positive in R/G, B/R and U/R (+2 to +3); flat in R/W, where you have your own 2/2s. Take it over any red common.
Hallway Heckler: Filler. 52.2%: a 3-mana rummager plus a 1-damage ping is too little for a slow format, as LLU's D+/C- predicted over LR's 'bread-and-butter' C. Only U/R (+1.9) gets value from the looting. It's negative in B/R (-2.1), its namesake ping deck, and in W/R. Take it in the last third of the pack.
Heartstring Puller: Solid filler four-drop: 54.7%, +0.7 IWD. Two bodies for four mana is fine but has no lasting impact in a stall-heavy format. It slightly helps U/R (+2.3) and is negative in R/G (-1.0), where your four slot wants ramp payoffs. LR 874 is right that it's a 'solid four' you won't rush to cut.
Identity Echo: Unplayable: both LR and LLU give it F, and a 3.2% play rate means no usable WR yet (provisional). Paying 4 each turn to swap a creature for a random one is pure variance with no card advantage. Don't take it.
Master of Barbs: Role-player, not the rare its B grade suggests: 53.1% GIH, +0.3 IWD. A menace 2/1 needs a steady stream of pings to matter. It fits U/R (+3.4) and is only flat in B/R (+1.0), its supposed home, and loses in R/G (-3.2). Play it in U/R or Stingerquill shells, but don't take it early.
No Admittance: Premium red removal: three damage for two kills about 68% of creatures, and the free Jace token adds a card's worth of value. At 56.7% it's the red common to take. Best in U/R (+4.4), where blue uses the token; middling in R/W and B/R. Easy to splash.
Pompous Battlemage: Filler one-drop. Prowess and aggro two-drops underperform here, and a 1/1 with a free loot drops off fast (51.7% when drawn). It's at least flat in U/R (+1.9). Its 56.2% OH WR comes from fast red starts, not from being a good card; take it late.
Pyre Rhymer: Trap. 50.5% GIH and -1.9 IWD: the format punishes prowess, and Molten Tide only gives you mana. The 3/3 body is fine, but it doesn't change the board. It's flat in U/R (+0.1) and negative in R/G (-2.5) and B/R (-3.3). Numot was right that it didn't need to be a rare. Take a removal spell instead.
Skilled Battlecarver: Filler two-drop: 52.9% with negative IWD in every pair (R/W −1.5). That is the format's aggro-two-drop trap in action. Only a dedicated R/W or near-mono-red aggro deck wants it, and those decks can pick it up late, as LoL said.
Stingcaster Mage: Strong pick, but not the slam a mythic Snapcaster suggests: 56.4% GIH with +2.5 IWD. It's best in U/R (+3.8) and B/R (+3.1), where cheap removal gives it rebuy targets, and flat in R/G (+0.6) with few spells. Take it early for spell-heavy red decks.
Tether Technician: Filler top-end. A 4/5 reach body that can trade a card for 2 damage is fine in a stalled board, but 52.6% puts it below the set median. It is near-neutral in R/G and U/R and negative in R/W (-1.4). That sides with Mark D+ over Numot's 'classic big red creature'. Take it as the 22nd-23rd card.
Violent Echoes: Premium removal: 59.3% GIH, +5.3 IWD. Six damage at instant speed kills anything, and against 3-toughness targets it draws a card through Jace. Best in U/R (+6.7) and B/R (+5.0), positive everywhere; take it over almost any common.
Wrath of the Bloodmane: Solid red removal: four damage kills most creatures, and it's often 2 mana with legends around. Its home is U/R (+3.6). It's flat in B/R, R/G and R/W, where other removal does the same job. Take it early but behind Fulminous Forte.
Arcane Amphisbaena: Solid green two-drop, the best one for G/U: +6.1 IWD there and 55.6% overall. The deathtouch body holds the stalled ground and pairs with fight spells, and the empower makes duals enter untapped. Roughly neutral in B/G, R/G and G/W (-0.9 to +0.8), so it's a high pick only for blue-green.
Bestial Incursion: Solid green playable: 56.2%. Two 4/4 tramplers on one card beat the Jace-token chumps, and it's great to mill or discard. LoL's 'antithesis of the format' was wrong; LR 874 and LLU moved it up. Best in U/G (+4.3) and B/G (+2.8). Watch for Unsummon.
Budding Insurgent: Trap. A vanilla 3/3 for 3 whose sac mode rarely matters; Ways are the main targets. 50.7% with -1.7 IWD, worst in BG (-3.5) and WG (-2.4). Cheap bodies with no lasting impact lose here. Sideboard it in against enchantment-heavy decks.
Carnivorous Cultivator: Premium: 58.7% GIH, +5.5 IWD. A 2/3 deathtouch for two shuts down ground attacks in a format that stalls, and the prepared side helps self-mill. Positive in every green pair, best in G/U (+7.2) and G/W (+5.0). Take it early for any green deck.
Compel Brutality: Solid green removal that's much better in G/U (+5.0): there a high-loyalty Jace token deals 4–6 damage with no creature at risk. In other green pairs it's a normal bite spell, roughly flat in R/G and G/W. Take it early in G/U; elsewhere it's just a playable.
Flourishing Grapple: Bo1 sideboard hoser and a maindeck trap at 44.2% (small sample, 2.6% play rate). It's a 1-mana bite that only hits red or white targets, and green's fight effects are already discounted. Board it in against R/W or a white-heavy opponent only.
Gardenize: Unplayable. There's no live WR because almost nobody registers it (3.8% play rate), so this read is provisional, but every reviewer gave it an F/0. Three mana for no board effect that needs your creatures to die first is a full turn wasted in a format won by card advantage. Never maindeck it.
Greenhouse Propagator: Role-player at 54.4%, despite Numot and LoL calling it great. It earns its slot in G/W lifegain (+2.8) and G/U ramp (+2.9) as a 2/3 dork that gains life repeatably. It is negative in R/G and B/G, which have better ramp and bodies. Mid-pack pick.
Heartwood Crafter: Strong ramp: 56.7%. Its 62.3% OH vs 52.8% GD shows it's a turn-one card, not a topdeck. Surprisingly it's best in U/G (+5.2), feeding big empower turns, then R/G (+2.3) for turn-4 Bestial Incursion flashback. Take it early in green ramp decks.
Hexhaven Invigorator: Build-around, R/G only. It is +5.2 in R/G, where Heartwood tokens and heavy green make GGGG castable and blocking a 6/6 vigilance ramps you further. The 54.4% overall is dragged down by two-colour decks that can't cast it on time. Take it early only if you are near mono-green with 12+ green sources, per LR and LLU.
Hungering Puppetbeast: Bomb: 61.6% GIH, +9.0 IWD, +7 to +10.6 in every green pair, led by R/G (+10.6) and B/G (+10.3). It comes down as a hasty 6/6 or a hexproof threat that dodges sorcery removal. Slam it P1P1 and splash it if needed.
Hunter's Axe: Don't play it. A 51.2% GIH WR and 25.8% play rate back the 874 verdict: equipment is bad in a card-advantage-and-removal format, and it does nothing on defense. Mildly positive only in G/W go-wide (+1.2); negative in R/G and B/G.
Inspired Tethermage: Filler. 51.6%, negative in every non-U/G pair (R/G -3.2). It's a 3/2 that grows only off loyalty counters, and the 6-mana sink is slow. LoL frames it as a piece for the Jace ramp or Paradox lifegain decks; even in G/U it's just +1.4. LLU's D+ was right. Use it as the 23rd card if you lack mana sinks.
Omnipresence: Unplayable (provisional, no live WR, 0.5% play rate). Eight mana does nothing on its own and needs a board you'd already be winning with. Every reviewer gave it a zero. Never take it.
Puppet Crafting: Build-around that doesn't work: 51.3% with a 48.2% OH WR. You need 6-7 artifact or non-Aura enchantment targets (Eye of Jace, Ways), and few decks have them. LR's D is closer than DS 3.0. Only for RG with plenty of targets (+0.4).
Restore with Empathy: Role-player whose value depends on the pair: 54.8% GIH overall, but +6.2 in G/U, where it rebuys walkers and bombs, and roughly zero in G/W, B/G and R/G. The 57.4% GD vs 50.3% OH marks it as a late-game card. Play it in G/U; elsewhere it's the 23rd card.
Simulacrum Shaper: First-pick rare: 59.8%, +6.6 IWD and 63.2% opening-hand WR. It ramps, fixes a splash, and replaces itself. Positive in every green pair and huge in G/U (+9.5) and B/G (+6.7). Only Craftwork Crusher beats it in R/G ramp decks.
Something Worth Saving: Undervalued glue that wheels (ALSA 6.9 for a 56.8% card). It smooths draws, finds bombs and fills the yard, which LR 876 and LLU 259 both singled out. Best in G/U (+2.0) and B/G (+1.8); flat in R/G (-0.5), where you'd rather ramp.
Sureshot Sower: Filler. 53.4% GIH and -0.8 IWD: a 3/1 two-drop that trades with tokens and 1/3s but falls off late. The flyer-killing mode keeps it alive against W/U. It's roughly neutral in G/U (+0.9) and worst in R/G (-2.7). LLU's 'mostly just filler' matches the data. Play it as a 22nd or 23rd card, never a priority pick.
Tarmogoyf: Solid playable (56.5%, +4.9) that usually plays as a 2-mana 3/4 to 4/5 that holds the ground well. B/G graveyard decks (+6.4) fill both yards fastest and get the most from it; it is only fine in R/G (+1.8). Take it over most green commons.
Tethermage's Advantage: Sideboard. 50.9% with an 8.3% play rate. Green pump tricks don't pay off in a removal-and-card-draw format, and it's -2.8 in R/G, its supposed home. Only main it if a green deck is desperate for interaction against fliers.
Verdant Kraken: Bomb-level payoff that wins whenever it resolves. At 57.8% with +5.8 IWD it is positive in every green pair, best in G/U (+7.6) and G/W (+6.6). The 60.1% GD vs 53.7% OH shows it rewards a slow game, and this format is slow. Slam it. The 7-mana cost is real, but the format reaches turn 7 often.
Vinelasher Adept: Solid playable that beat its grades: 55.5% GIH, +1.7 IWD. Turn-2 landcycling is never a dead card, and the late counters put a flier or blocker out of reach. Best in G/U (+3.5); flat in R/G (-0.2). A good mid-pack pick, not a priority.
Wrecking Gecko: Filler fatty that plays better than its 0.5 DS grade: ward 2 dodges a lot of the format's removal and the mana sink ends stalls. Best in G/U (+4.2) and B/G (+2.5); a late pick for your 5-drop slot, not an early take.
Aerid Konstrari: Bomb — first-pick it. 64.4% with +13.1 IWD, and +14.4 in R/G. A 4-mana 5/4 flier that leaves a Heartwood when it enters and when it dies outclasses everything in a format where boards stall on the ground. LR's A+ was right. It pulls you hard into R/G (Konstrari, 55.2%).
Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes: Premium, near-first-pick, but only in G/U: 60.1%, +8.8 IWD, a set-high +12.6 in G/U. A 2/3 on turn 2 that Empowers 2 on every land drip-feeds cards in a format won by card advantage. It lifts G/U, the worst archetype at 52.7%. LR's 'slam' beats LLU's B.
Blessed Ghoul: Filler you play for synergy. 54.1%, but 55.9% OH vs 52.8% GD shows it is just an early drop. It earns a slot only with self-mill or sacrifice: UB/WB (+2.3/+1.8). Negative in WR (-2.9) and BG/BR. LoL 500 says never pick it for its own sake. Late pick.
Bloombrute: Premium gold uncommon: 57.4% GIH, +4.8 IWD, +5.1 in G/W, where it's among that pair's best cards. Repeatable lifegain turns a 4/4 into a card each turn, and that's what G/W needs most (4 payoffs for 18 sources). LR's A− beats Mark's C. Take it once you lean G/W.
Charge the Sanctum: Sideboard card: 50.6% at a 13% play rate. A three-mana pump spell is weak in a slow format with five sweepers, and it's negative in R/W (−1.4), the deck it was made for. The U/R +3.0 is small-sample noise. Play it only as a 23rd card in go-wide aggro.
Clash of Elements: Premium gold removal: a 3-mana instant answer to any nonland permanent at 58.4%. Opponents mostly take the 2 damage and redraw it, which is still fine tempo in a slow game. +5.4 in U/B splashes and +4.5 in U/R. Pick it over mono-colour commons.
Craftwork Crusher: Bomb uncommon. Only a handful of rares post a higher WR. 62.0% GIH and +8.8 IWD: a 7/5 trampler that kills something and draws or makes a body is exactly what a slow format rewards. It's strongest in G/U (+12.2), and the hybrid-heavy cost still pays off in R/G (+8.7) and B/G (+7.7). Take it early and build ramp around it.
Denzilore Fatehold: Bomb: 61.5% with +11.7 IWD in W/U, the best pair, where surveil turns every Jace activation into a team pump. It is still great in U/B (+7.6). Flash matters less than it reads, but a 4-mana 3/4 flier is good even without triggers. Slam it and move into W/U.
Desperate Futurescribe: Premium W/U gold card: 57.6% with +4.7 IWD in W/U. A 4-mana 3/4 flier is already above rate, and a Jace token surveil grows a creature every turn. It also travels to U/B (+2.6). Take it early if you're in or near Fatehold.
Emergency Phytomedic: Solid role-player. Its 54.2% sits near the median, and it is positive in all six pairs it appears in (+1.0 to +1.9). That makes it a flexible 1-drop that grows itself and feeds G/W lifegain counters. LR 874: playable in synergy decks, weaker in Sealed. Take it mid-pack as glue, not as a priority.
Entrust the Spark: Unplayable: F from LR and LLU, 1.4% play rate, no live data. Jace tokens are not cards in your library, so it needs real planeswalker cards to find. Leave it in the pack; this read is provisional only in the sense that no sample exists.
Fatehold Charm: Premium W/U gold card and among the pair's best uncommons (57.8%). Draw-plus-Jace is the floor, remanding a key spell is the blowout, and the team pump wins go-wide combats. A 54.3% OH WR shows it's more value than tempo; take it once you're W/U.
Fatehold Chronologist: Solid hybrid common (56.3%): a 1/2 flier now and a 2/2 plus surveil later, so it fills the curve on its own (LR's B- beat LLU's C). Positive in nearly every blue or white pair, best in G/U (+4.4) and U/B (+2.9), only -0.5 in R/W. A safe early pick that keeps you open between white and blue.
Ferocity of the Hunt: Filler-minus; usually leave it out. 52.8% sits below deck average in nearly every pair. Its only homes are blue value decks, U/G (+4.8) and U/B (+4.6). There it goes on small ETB two-for-ones like Oculus or Rank Rat, per LoL 500, never to protect a big threat. Take LR's negative read over LoL 499's 'good'.
Frostbite Pyromental: Trap. A haste Ball Lightning that draws two is great on turn 3 and dead in a stalled turn-7 board; 50.7% overall and -0.9 in UR. LR's D was right. Only for an aggressive UR curve, and even there it is the last red card.
Grim Repriser: Filler two-drop: 53.2% GIH, -1.2 IWD, and -1.0 even in B/R, its home pair. Prowess bodies and recursion that needs noncombat damage that turn underperform in a slow format. It's playable in B/R aggro if you're already there, but don't move into the colours for it, as LLU says.
Ingris Stingerquill: Bomb for B/R: +5.4 IWD there, and it's the only reason to want the pair. A 1/4 flier blocks well early, every attacker pings, and the {4} Cadets give it a late-game mana sink. Its 57.3% sits in the premium tier. With BRR in the cost, it's hard to splash, so take it only if you're open to B/R.
Konstrari Charm: Solid R/G playable (55.9%, +2.1 in R/G), better than Numot's "worst charm" call. The counters-plus-trample mode is the real card; the 6-damage flier kill is a strong backup against W/U, and the mana mode helps ramp into Colossus or Kiora. Mid-pack pick.
Konstrari Improviser: Filler. 53.9% GIH and -0.3 IWD. A 2/2 that later makes a Heartwood keeps your curve smooth but has no lasting impact. It's near zero in G/U and U/R and negative in R/W (-3.2) and B/R (-2.7). LR's 874 'up' call is fair only relative to Woodwork Prodigy. It's a fine ramp piece in R/G, but pick it mid-pack.
Kwia Vigorbloom: Bomb: 62.0% with +11.2 IWD. A 6/6 flier with vigilance, lifelink and ward 2 takes over a board stall by itself, so it beats LLU's 'worst sphinx' A−. Best in G/W (+12.6) and still +10 when splashed into W/U. First-pick it.
Mind Meanderer: Premium two-for-one: a 4/4 flier that fights on ETB. 57.3% GIH with 59.6% GD shows it wins long games, which this format is. It's +7.1 in U/B Sultai splashes and +6.9 in U/G. The awkward cost is its only flaw; worth a speculative pick.
Null Summoner: Bomb rare. First-pick quality. At 62.6% with +10.5 IWD it is among the set's best rares: it strips their best card for good and gives you a 4-power body. Absurd in U/B (+11.3), where threshold turns the stolen card into yours, and it still delivers +9.9 in W/U. LLU's A and LR's A- are confirmed. Slam it.
Paradox Shaper: Role-player that plays below its engine reputation: 54.9% GIH, +1.0 IWD. It belongs only in U/B (+2.5) as a 1/3 wall and mill engine; negative in U/R and B/G (-2.6). One copy is a fine late-game plan; three copies only for LSV-style removal-heavy deck-out builds.
Primal Witchstalker: Premium uncommon: a 3-mana 2/1 menace that ramps, hits land drops and fills the graveyard. 59% GIH, +4.7 IWD, and 61% OH says it's a strong early play. Strong in both U/B (+4.5) and B/G (+4.0); it's often passed 5th, so lean Sultai when you see it.
Proctor of Potential: Premium W/U rare: 60.1%, +6.5 IWD in W/U. The 3/1 trades, then returns from the graveyard once you've surveilled, and it surveils itself whenever another creature enters. LR's B+ is about right. Narrow because of its gold cost, but worth an early pick toward W/U (Fatehold, the top pair at 56.4%).
Prudent Fateseer: Solid playable: 55.7%. Two bodies and a surveil from one card, and the 1/4 holds the ground in a stall-heavy format. Best in U/B (+4.9), where it's a durable blocker. It's fine in W/U (+2.9) and negative in white aggro (W/G -1.5, R/W -2.0). The +1/+0 rarely matters; value it as a blocker plus a Cadet.
Recursive Recruitment: Premium uncommon, splashable. Two 2/2s soak attacks and protect Jace, then the flashback makes two large finishers late. 60.5% with +6.0 IWD, huge in UG/UR/UB (+7.4/+6.6/+6.5), and live as a splash. It was upgraded post-release toward A-. Take it over most commons in any blue deck.
Solarium Sentry: Solid playable: 55.9% GIH, +4.1 IWD in G/W. Most of the value is a 2-mana 3/3 that holds the ground (59.0% OH). The 2-life triggers are a small bonus, as LLU says, so it lands below LR's B+. A good early play for G/W, not a first pick.
Solitary Cell: Overrated rare: 50.6% and flat in R/W (−0.4) despite B grades. Exiling a permanent of mana value 3 or less misses the four- and five-drops that decide this slow format, and it costs two colours. It can still hit a Jace token. Play it in R/W, but take a playable creature over it.
Stingerquill Charm: Good flexible removal, but the B+ grades overrate it. At 55.2% it's only +1.4 in B/R, the bottom-tier pair it's locked into, which is why Alex dropped it. A Bolt plus two other modes is still a clear take once you're in B/R.
Stingerquill Voxmancer: Role-player. 54.2% GIH and +1.7 IWD: a 1-drop that's annoying because nothing cheap answers it, but it isn't powerful. Surprisingly, it's best in U/R (+3.6), ahead of B/R (+2.6). The data contradicts LLU's 'most important combo card' claim, so take it only when you have real ping payoffs.
Stinging Vitriol: Filler: 53.0% and only +0.8 in B/R, the one pair that plays it. Two damage plus a Thoughtseize helps the ping deck, but it adds no board presence in a grindy format. Run it in B/R as a noncombat-damage enabler, never splash it, and don't take it early.
Tam's Resistance: Sleeper. It plays well above the 1.0 DS grade at 56.1% because Empower 4 is a 2-mana cantrip on a hybrid cost. It's +6.0 in U/B and +5.7 in U/G but -0.8 in R/G, so it's really a blue card. Run it out turn 2 and pick it mid-pack in any blue deck.
Tenured Tethermage: Premium R/G rare. At 58.7% with +6.2 IWD (R/G +6.4), it ramps you two lands ahead and becomes an instant-speed growing threat once the Heartwoods untap. It is the engine that feeds Kiora and Craftwork Crusher. LLU's A-/B+ fits the data better than LR's B. Take it early and pull toward R/G.
Theorix Charm: Strong U/B playable, better than LLU's C+: 57.0% GIH, +3.8 IWD, +3.7 in U/B. Each mode is inefficient, but in a slow format the flexibility of counter, kill-a-2-toughness, or dig always has a target. Take it early once you are U/B.
Theorix Metamage: Filler in U/B (+1.8) that LoL now calls the main evasive threat of rareless U/B: mill 3 into a 3/3 flyer at threshold. Don't play it outside self-mill, especially in B/R (-4.2). A late pick that fills the 3-slot.
Twinned Vision: Premium card draw: 57.9% and the format's best draw spell per LLU's upgrade (take it 4th-5th pick). Best in U/B (+3.4) and U/R (+3.3); because it's hybrid, red decks can play it too. LR's Gruul point holds (+1.6pp above the R/G average). Weak in R/W (-1.6). Hold a land in hand so you can flash it back.
Twisted Fates: Premium removal if you're W/B or W/U with a black splash: 56.9%, +4.5 IWD. It kills any nonland permanent, walkers included, and pumps your team, a 'last card cast' finisher. It's strongest in W/U (+6.0), though the WWB cost is hard to splash. It's bad in R/W (-2.6), which can't pay for it.
Uldaros Theorix: Bomb: slam it. 69.2% with +19.2 IWD, and +22.9 in UB, the biggest swing in the chunk. A 6-mana 5/5 flier that recasts removal or a landcycler for free is a two- or three-for-one. Worth pulling you into UB from any seat.
Vigorbloom Charm: Solid G/W playable: 56.4% GIH, +3.4 in G/W. The fight mode is green's best removal mode here, and draw-plus-3-life feeds the lifegain payoffs. The best of a weak pack, as LoL puts it, but don't splash it. Take it mid-pack once you're G/W.
Vigorbloom Vanguard: Solid playable at 56.2%, well above its 1.5 grade. It's effectively a three-mana 3/3 that gains life, positive in every white pair: W/B +4.2, G/W +3.5, W/U +2.9. The hybrid cost lets white decks play it; it's flat in R/G and B/G. Battalion (57.4%) is slightly better.
Vindictive Triumph: Premium removal in U/B, merely solid in W/B. At 54.1% overall the BBW cost hurts, but it's +8.7 IWD in U/B splashes against +1.6 in the weak W/B deck. Instant exile for anything; cast it at end of turn to steal and attack with a cheap creature.
Warrior's Blades: Solid playable. Lightning Helix stapled to a lasting equipment. 54.6% GIH, but +3.4 IWD says it lifts whatever deck plays it. Oddly it does better in W/G (+4.4) and W/U (+3.8) than in R/W (+2.5), so it plays best as a splashed removal spell, not as an aggro anchor. LR's B is about right.
Whiplash Wordsmith: Trap: 49.5% and −2.3 to −2.7 IWD in every red pair. A 5-mana 3/3 that only flies on turns you ping is awful on defense in a slow format. LLU's D+ was right and LR's C/C+ was too kind. Leave it in the sideboard even in B/R.
Woodwork Prodigy: Filler that plays worse than it reads. 52.3% GIH, flat IWD everywhere and -2.2 in R/G, its home. LSV is right that the second Heartwood matters far less than the first. A 3-mana 3/3 is fine early but loses late; take R/G payoffs over it.
Afterthought Sentry: Filler. Don't take it before pick 10. At 53.0% with -1.4 IWD it is negative in B/R (-2.6) and R/G (-2.3), the decks that supposedly want an artifact 2-drop. It is roughly neutral in U/R and U/B. A 2/2 body falls off in this format and the graveyard hate rarely matters. LR's D and LLU's D+ are confirmed.
Archive Arbiter: Solid colourless playable, above its grades: 55.9% GIH, +2.9 IWD, positive in seven of eight pairs, best in U/B (+5.5). A 6-mana flier that kills a Jace token, Way, or removal enchantment fits the stalled format. Run one in control decks; skip it in R/G (-0.5).
Codie, Ravenous Codex: Trap. 46.9% GIH and -3.2 IWD; it needs about three re-preparing creatures, and the five-colour ability almost never comes online. A 1/4 for 3 blocks OK but does nothing on its own. Only for a W/U Peer Review deck that already has the engines, and even then it's the 23rd card.
The Echoverse Fulcrum: Premium in U/B, beating LR's C and LLU's C/D+. 58.4% overall with +9.7 in U/B, where a colorless loot plus a telegraphed 5-mana wipe suits the removal-and-two-for-ones control deck. Any colour can play it. Strongest in decks with few creatures; aggressive white decks should pass it.
Eye of Jace: Don't play it: 49.8%, negative in both W/U and U/B. One mana for surveil 1 per turn adds nothing in a set full of surveil. The 2-point drain arrives far too late. LLU 259 and LR's dismissal win out over Numot.
Keeper of the Quiet Hour: Solid colourless filler that beats its DS 0.5. A 3/2 that empowers Jace and turns duals untapped is worth more than it reads at 56.1%. It belongs in blue: UG +4.4, UB +3.1. Negative in WG/WR/BR (-3.4/-2.8/-2.4). Mid pick in blue decks only.
Living Library: Sideboard card that you can play as the 23rd. 52.9% GIH, and it hurts in W/U (-4.6). A 0/4 doesn't hold back much and the 6-mana removal is very slow, though it does shield your walkers early. Only 11% of decks play it. Take it last, as LoL and LR both say.
Medic's Kitesail: Role-player at 54.3% that breaks board stalls by giving a big ground creature flying. Best in G/W (+3.8) and B/G (+2.5), where green bodies carry it and each attack gains life. Flat in R/W. Play one copy, never two; it goes late (ALSA 7.1).
Murmuring Volume: Quietly good glue for slow multicolour decks (56.3%), well above LLU's C−; LR 876 and SotF upgraded it. Ramp plus repeatable looting wins long games: +3.6 in G/U and +3.0 in U/R. Skip it in W/U (-1.0) and W/B (-2.6) aggro shells.
Dedicated Commons: Splash-only land. 52.8% GIH, +0.1 IWD. Outside blue it's a tapland, which shows in -2.4 in R/W itself. It's slightly positive in W/U (+2.1), where Jace tokens untap it. Take it late, and play it only to support a real red or white splash.
Deserted Beach: Fine fixing but a low pick. The 55.3% GIH reflects W/U, the best pair, rather than the land itself: W/U IWD is −0.9, and the ten common duals already enter untapped with a planeswalker out. Play it in W/U or a W/U splash, and take spells over it.
Fatehold Annex: Good only in blue decks that make Jace tokens, which let it enter untapped: +6.1 in U/G and +4.9 in U/R (as a splash land), but only +0.3 in W/U itself. Take it mid-pack for a blue splash. Outside blue it's a tapland.
Formidable Commons: Take it late, and only for blue decks or a real splash. Its 55.4% comes from U/B (+2.3) and G/U (+2.1), where Jace tokens let it enter untapped. In actual B/G it is -2.8 because it plays as a tapland. Pick it for a Sultai splash or a blue shell, and skip it in a straight B/G deck.
Hall of Echoes: Filler land: 53.0% GIH, +0.1 IWD, splitting LR's B and LLU's C-. The 5-mana activation is too slow to matter in most games, and the colourless mana hurts double-pip decks. Play it only in slower two-colour decks with light colour requirements.
Haunted Ridge: Take it late, play it only for a real splash. 55.1% is exactly the mean, and it's negative in B/R (-2.7), where red-black's untapped plays matter. It's a non-blue dual with no Jace synergy; the rare slowland adds little over the commons.
Hexhaven Dueling Arena: Don't play it. 49.9%, -2.3 IWD, 13% play rate, and negative even in W/U, the one pair with enough data. LR's F prediction ('I would bet the win rate is negative') was right. A colorless land is a real cost, and re-preparing creatures is too slow and expensive to be worth it.
Innovative Commons: Take it fairly late, but it's one of the better duals: 56.0%. It plays untapped once you have a Jace token. Best in blue decks that make tokens all game: U/G (+4.7), U/B (+3.1), W/U (+2.5). In R/G (-1.8) and B/R (-2.8) it's just a tapland. Play it there only for a real splash.
Konstrari Annex: Dual that wants blue Jace decks, not RG. The 54.3% hides a split: +5.3 in UG and +3.8 in UR as a splash enabler that enters untapped, but -3.3 in RG, where it is a tapland. Take it late, and only to splash or with a Jace engine.
Meticulous Commons: Dual that's only good in blue decks: +3.2 in U/B and +1.9 in W/U, where Jace tokens make it enter untapped, but negative in W/B, B/G and G/W. 54.2% GIH is filler. Take it late; outside blue, play it only for a real white or black splash.
Overgrown Farmland: Tapland outside blue: 53.0% with 0.0 IWD, and −3.4 in G/W, its own pair. G/W rarely has a planeswalker to make lands enter untapped, so it often comes in tapped and slows the curve. Take it late and play it only to fix a real splash.
Rockfall Vale: Replacement-level R/G dual (55.1%, +1.7 in R/G). Outside blue it rarely enters untapped through a planeswalker, and the 'two other lands' rule makes it a tapland early. Take it late for the R/G mana base or a red/green splash; never early.
Roiling Canopy: Unplayable. 49.0% GIH and -1.1 IWD: a tapped Forest whose trigger needs six Forests, so you won't see it before turn 7. Even mono-green gets almost nothing from +3/+3. Every expert gave it an F, and the data agrees. Play a basic Forest instead.
Room of Refuge: Splash enabler that beats the C+ read in blue: G/U +3.0, U/B +2.3, but negative in R/G (−2.4), B/G and W/B, where it is a tapland that costs tempo. Take it mid-pack for a real splash, especially in Sultai B/G/u. The 5-mana counters mode is a late-game bonus.
Shipwreck Marsh: Good dual: 57.7% with +3.1 IWD, usually untapped from turn 3 without needing a planeswalker. Oddly it's best in W/U (+5.3) as a black splash, then U/B (+3.6). Pick it over most filler when you're blue with black in view.
Stingerquill Annex: Trap in its own colours. In B/R it is -4.0 and in R/G -2.8 because without blue planeswalker support it is a tapland. Only U/R (+3.5) gets value, as the splash or untapped dual. The 53.9% is below the median. Pick it late only for a blue splash; otherwise pass it.
Theorist's Sanctum: Premium for blue: 57.7% GIH, +4.4 IWD, and a free include, since it costs a blue deck almost nothing. Strongest in Jace-heavy G/U (+7.3) and W/U (+5.6). Take it early in any blue deck; it turns flood into card draw.
Theorix Annex: Good dual for blue decks (56.4%), where Jace tokens often make it enter untapped. Best in G/U (+3.5) and W/U (+2.4) as the splash land; negative in B/G and B/R, where it's a tapland. Take it mid-pack for U/x splashes.
Transformative Commons: Good only in blue decks: +3.6 in G/U, +3.0 in U/B, +2.6 in U/R, but negative in R/G (-0.5) and B/G (-1.4), where it's just a tapland. Blue makes the most Jace tokens, so it usually enters untapped. 55.9% overall. Take it mid-pack in G/U; outside blue, play it only for a real splash.
Vigorbloom Annex: Late pick, tapland outside blue: 53.0%, -0.8 IWD, negative in its own G/W (-2.5) and in U/G. G/W makes few Jace tokens, so it rarely enters untapped. Play it only to make a real splash work. Ignore TCG's 3.5 blanket grade on duals.
Ajani Resolute: Trap rare: don't take it early. A 2-mana walker that can't protect itself and rarely makes a Pridemate. 52.6% overall and flat even in WG (-0.2). LSV and LLU called it right. Play it only in a committed WG lifegain deck, and never start one for it.
Danitha, Sword of Hope: Build-around trap in most decks: 52.0% GIH and negative in every pair, worst in W/U (-3.6). The WR reflects decks with 4–5 targeting effects; it needs 9–10 (Blades, tricks, Seed Suture). LR 874's 'No, I'm good' is the right default. Play it only in a W/R or G/W deck full of targeting spells.
Ghalta the Immovable: Late-pick niche card: 52.0% overall, but +4.4 in W/U, where high-toughness surveil creatures make it cheap. LLU calls it a 20th–23rd card, not a deck to build around. Outside W/U it's often stuck in hand, so leave it in the pack.
Gideon's Memorial: Trap at 50.8% (-1.9 IWD) despite going around pick 4. It's really a 2-mana cycling 4-damage combat trick; the token anthem only matters in R/W go-wide, and it's -3.7 in G/W. Play it only as a removal stand-in for R/W token decks.
Koth of the Homestead: Role-player for G/W. 54.0% GIH, +1.4 IWD. It's a source of free repeatable lifegain, which Vigorbloom needs, at +2.4 in G/W. It's slightly negative in W/B and R/W. LoL's 'good in lifegain, bad elsewhere' beats Numot's 'insane'. Take it mid-pack for G/W, and pass it otherwise.
Liliana the Faultless: Premium in G/W (+6.5): repeatable lifegain is exactly what Vigorbloom's four payoffs need, and the hexproof mode protects your best threat. The 61.4% opening-hand WR shows it wants to be on the board early. Still good in W/U (+4.6). This lands closer to Alex's B+ than Mark's B−.
Lyra, Archangel of Dawn: Premium: 58.8% with +5.3 IWD. A single-pip 3-mana 3/3 flier is a strong floor, and lifegain grows it. It's +8.4 in G/W (repeatable gain) and +6.7 in W/B, so the data beats LLU's C+ downgrade. Take it early in any white deck.
Rescue Girl, First Responder: Build-around that is a trap in most decks. At 52.5% it is negative in every white pair and worst in R/W (-4.4). LLU 259's bar is right: you need about two rare ETB payoffs (Lich's Relic, Vraska, Ajani's Anguish) or multiple Hapatras before a 3-mana 1/3 earns a slot. Without those, it stays in the sideboard.
Saheeli, Consul of Oversight: Role-player at the mean: 55.1% GIH, +1.4 IWD, below its 3.5 grade. LLU's read holds: without a Jace token out she is mostly an Air Elemental. Play her in W/U (+2.4) surveil decks; she is a trap in R/W (-4.8).
Teyo, Lightshield Expert: Solid two-drop that beats its rate: flash hexproof blanks removal, the counter is permanent, and the loyalty mode turns Jace into a draw. Best in W/U (+4.3) and W/B (+2.9); negative in R/W (-1.8), where a 1/1 flash body is a weak aggro drop.
Thalia, the Survivor: Role-player (54.5%). LR's 874 read holds: a fine white playable you'd never cut, but not one to chase. The 3/4 lifelink body and tax on removal and counterspells are best in W/U (+4.1) and G/W (+3.0), the slow and lifegain decks. Negative in R/W (-2.1), because aggro doesn't use the tax. Take it mid-pack.
Tomik, Orzhov Lawmage: Filler two-drop: 53.9%, flat or negative in every white pair (best W/B 0.0). A 2/1 flier is below the power bar in this slow, stall-heavy format, and the walker protection rarely matters. LoL's read beats LLU's B- and DS's optimism. Fine in a W/U fliers deck, never an early pick.
Way of the Healer: Premium: the best Way. A Jace that makes a 2/2 Cadet every -2 is a steady token stream that stalls boards and digs. 57.3% with +4.0 IWD, peaking in WU (+5.4) and UB (+4.9); it fades in WG (-0.8). It reaches A- with 5-7 other empower cards. Early pick in W/U.
Way of the Mentor: Weak Way, and the WR backs Alex's D−: 50.3% GIH, -0.7 IWD. Three mana that doesn't touch the board is a slow Divination. Only W/B is slightly positive (+1.7), and lifegain decks want to attack, not tick up Jace. Play it as the 23rd card at most.
Yoshimaru, Beloved Companion: Trap: 49.6% and negative in every white pair, worst in W/B (−4.9) and R/W (−4.6). The LoL host's favourite has numbers to match LLU's D grade. +1/+1 counters underperform in this set, and a three-mana 2/2 does nothing by itself. Pass it even in counter decks.
Yuriko, Blade of the Mighty: Filler (53.0%) with a swingy ceiling. The 4-mana 2/3 does nothing on entry, but the double strike for lone attackers punishes stalls in G/W (+3.2), its best home. Elsewhere it's barely above replacement; LLU's D grade is closer than LR's C.
Arni, Humble Scribe: Role-player. 54.3% GIH and +1.4 IWD: free repeatable looting is real value in a long format, but the 2-toughness body dies easily. Best in U/B (+2.7) for threshold and G/U (+2.5), and slightly negative in W/U (-1.2). LLU's C range is more accurate than LR's B+. Pick it as a mid-pack playable.
Chandra, Chill of Compliance: Near-bomb at 59.0% (+6.1), well above LLU's C: a 3-mana walker that stun-locks their best creature, then surveils every turn. Best in W/U (+6.1), where each +1 triggers surveil payoffs, and strong in U/B (+5.3). Take it early in blue.
Fblthp, Impossibly Lost: Strong blue card, but its 59.7% is inflated: redraws after shuffling back count as extra wins. It's still a cheap draw-two that blue triggers easily, positive in every blue pair (+7.6 in U/B, where the empty-library win matters). LR's reversal stands; take it highly in blue.
Geist of Saint Thalia: Solid playable that beats its pre-data grades. At 56.8% with +3.5 IWD, a cheap flier that discounts blue's many noncreature draw and bounce spells works well in this card-draw format. Best in G/U (+5.6) and U/B (+4.2), and only marginal in W/U (+0.9). LR 874 called it 'good enough'. Numot and Mark undersold it.
Hapatra, the Desert Frost: Filler: 53.1% GIH, low 52.6% play rate, and 3 toughness dies to most removal. The exception is G/U (+5.6), where the tempo swing protects the Jace token; elsewhere she is a 23rd card. Take her late, not as a playable you need.
Jace, Reality Sculptor: First-pick rare in blue, much better than the LLU C grade: 57.9% with +5.8 IWD. The -3 buys a full turn in a stalled format, then each +1 empowers by your Island count. Huge in U/B (+7.7) and U/R (+6.2); you need 3+ Islands, so don't splash it.
Lyra, Tolarian Archangel: Bomb in blue: 60.8%, +8.5 IWD, and +10 or more in G/U and U/B. A 3-mana 3/3 flier dominates a ground-stalled format, and card draw like Twinned Vision regularly makes her extra Angel. Data backs LR's A- over LLU's B-. Opponents will hold removal for her, but take her first and play 10-11 blue sources for the UU.
Proft, Consulting Detective: Premium blue two-drop: 57.3%, +3.5 IWD, playable in every blue pair. It turns surveil into extra cards as the game goes long, exactly what this format rewards. It's best in U/G (+5.2) and U/B (+4.3), not just W/U surveil. It plays better than LLU's C because the late-game pay-2 draws decide stalls.
Ruric Thar, Biomagus: Solid top-end, better than LLU's C-. A 6-mana 4/6 flier that draws when targeted is a good finisher in a slow format; 57.8% GD vs 51.1% OH confirms a late-game card. Huge in UG (+7.8) and UB (+5.2), barely matters in WU (+0.6). Take it mid-pack in blue.
Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun: Sideboard card: 48.1% GIH, -3.8 IWD. A 2/1 for two is the whole main-deck value. Split second only matters against counterspell-heavy blue opponents, but in Bo1 you rarely know that ahead of time. LLU's sideboard read holds up. Don't main-deck it.
Tetsuko Umezawa, Fugitive: Solid blue two-drop at 54.6%. The 1/3 body holds the ground and unblockable small creatures attack Jace tokens. Best in G/U (+3.3) with small creatures and its own Jace plan, and still positive in other blue pairs. A mid-pack pick; it gets better the more X/1s you have.
Traxos, Academy Guardian: Solid blue playable (55.6%). It's often a 2-mana 1/5 flying wall that protects Jace and blocks the format's fliers. Strong in U/B (+5.0) and G/U (+5.3), flat in U/R (+0.1) despite prowess. Alex's B− holds up better than Mark's C.
Way of the Cryomancer: Filler, niche. 52.9% GIH, +0.4 IWD. Its spell-copy mode is rarely better than Jace's own -3 draw, so it plays as a 3-mana surveil-and-draw. It's slightly positive only in G/U (+2.3), and only with 7-8 removal or token spells to copy (LLU 259). LR's D is the right grade. Skip it outside the Jace package.
Way of the Mind Sculptor: Premium blue engine. The post-release notes (LR 874, LLU's SotF) flipped it to a top-two Way, and 57.8% with +5.1 IWD backs that up. In G/U (+8.2) and U/B (+5.8) it draws a card off every Jace −3 and decides slow games. The pre-data DS 0.5 and D+ grades were wrong.
Yargle, Goliath of Otaria: Unplayable main deck: 46.8% with a 4.1% play rate. A vanilla 5-mana 3/9 does nothing in a format won by card advantage. It's a Bo3 sideboard wall against R/G ground beats at most.
Yuriko, Hope from the Shadows: Filler 1-drop. At 53.3% it is below the median. It does best in U/B (+2.6), where a full graveyard makes the -X/-0 mode a real combat answer and surveil 2 feeds threshold. Elsewhere it is a 1/1 flash cantrip-lite. It is fine as a 22nd card in U/B, which sides with Marshall's C- over LSV's enthusiasm.
Danitha, Spear of Agony: Trap: 50.5% GIH, -0.4 IWD. A 3-mana 2/2 grows too slowly in a format that stalls by turn 5. Only W/B and U/B (+2.1 to +2.2) tolerate it; B/G (-5.5) and B/R (-2.4) lose with it. LR's B is too high; take something else.
Gallia, Tragic Host: Solid two-drop: a 2/1 menace early that recurs as a late mana sink, which fixes the problem of cheap bodies falling off. Best in W/B (+2.2), where it fills the aggro curve; slightly negative in B/G, where it competes for graveyard creatures. Mid-pick.
Garruk, Veiled Butcher: Bomb — slam it and splash it. 65.9% with +13.3 IWD, the highest numbers in this group. It's +15.9 in B/G, +14.3 in U/B and +12.7 even in B/R, the weakest black pair. It takes over the board for many turns, and the -2 or the +2 handles most boards in a slow format. LR and LLU rated it A, and the data agrees.
Gideon the Oathless: Premium three-drop, a pick over most removal: 59.2%, +6.5 IWD. Ward-discard forces a two-for-one, and the pings add up against Jace activations. Best in W/B (+10.5), B/R (+7.1) and U/B (+6.8). LR's 'take over Extended Absence' matches the data, so trust it over B grades.
Liliana the Repentant: Solid rare for BG. Early body, steady mill, and a late reanimation fit the recursion deck: +4.1 in BG, +1.2 in UB, negative in WB/BR. 56.2% overall. The mill is mandatory, so watch your library in long games. LR 874 prefers Oculus. Good pick if you are BG.
Loot, the Anomaly: Trap: 47.8% GIH, -2.9 IWD, in only 11% of decks. It plays as a vanilla 2/4, since threshold is a side plan and there's no sacrifice deck to feed it. Even its home pair, U/B, is slightly negative (-0.5). Leave it in the sideboard.
Mabel, Bitter Recluse: Filler with a matchup-dependent ETB: 53.6%, flat IWD. Killing a Jace token pays off in U/B (+2.1), where control can grind out the value. It's negative in B/R and W/B (−2.9 each), where a 1/1 falls off the board. Take it for U/B; otherwise take it late.
Massacre Girl, Most Wanted: Trap: 49.9% as a 5-mana 4/4 whose drains don't add up. LLU's "drain effects are very overrated" beats LR's B. Flat to negative in every pair (-2.7 in W/B, where it looks best on paper). Take removal or card draw instead.
Proft, Sinister Mastermind: Solid playable for U/B. 54.4% GIH, +1.7 IWD, and a 56.0% drawn WR versus 51.6% in the opening hand shows it's a late-game card. Early it's a -3/-1 removal spell, and once you reach threshold it's a 3-mana 5/5 menace. Best in U/B (+2.6), flat in B/R. LR's B is generous, but both halves play.
Teyo, Diamondblade Mage: Trap: 50.6% and below median almost everywhere. B/R (−3.1) and W/B (−2.0) are bad, and it is barely positive in U/B and B/G. A 4-mana 3/1 whose deathtouch and counter overlap is a mediocre flash trick at best. Agree with LR's D. Take it late, if at all.
Tinybones, Pocket Nuisance: Solid playable: 55.3% with +3.1 IWD. A 3-mana two-for-one with discard plus pings fits the attrition decks: +5.4 in W/B and +4.1 in U/B, near flat in B/R and B/G. Mid-pack pick for black control shells.
Way of the Deathbringer: Niche, below median. At 51.3% it is best in U/B (+2.2) as 'draw a card, keep a Jace', and in B/R it is a trap (-3.2). The sac-for-4/4 mode needs disposable bodies like Rank Rat or Gallia, which most decks lack. LoL 500 and LR agree: it doesn't fit the Empower plan. Take it late, and only in U/B.
Way of the Necromancer: Unplayable: 43.7% GIH, -4.2 IWD, the bottom of the set. Ben and LR both recanted; LLU calls it tied for worst. It costs a card for a weak Jace bump. Never maindeck it.
Winter, Tormented Loner: Role-player that needs fodder: sacrificing a spent Jace token makes the edict real removal. Good in B/G (+2.4) and U/B (+1.7), which have graveyard creatures and tokens; avoid it in B/R (-2.8). Low-quality removal at 53.7%, so pick it mid-to-late.
Yargle, Glutton of Urborg: Unplayable. 45.1% on a tiny 2.1% play rate (small sample, but every expert agreed). A 5-mana 9/3 with no text trades with any two-drop, dies to 3 damage, and gets chump-blocked by Jace tokens. Never take it.
Ajani Unrelenting: Slam it in any deck; bonus-sheet bomb and best card in the set: 73.2%, +20.4 IWD. Even in R/G, U/R and B/R it gains about +20 everywhere. The one-sided sweeper plus a Cadet on every loyalty activation wins games alone. Splash it if you must.
Arni, Renowned Champion: Trap: one of the worst cards in the set at 46.3% with -3.3 IWD, -4.5 in RG. A 1/5 that needs a creature entering to attack is a defensive body in a deck that wants threats. LLU's D- is correct. Don't play it.
Chandra, Torch of Defiance: Bomb: 59.9% GIH, +6.9 IWD. She kills a creature for 4 the turn she lands, then pulls ahead by drawing cards or pinging. Best in U/R (+10.0), and still +5 or more in R/G and B/R. Take her first and play her in any red deck.
Gallia, the Merrymaker: Trap: 50.6% and negative in every pair, worst in U/R (−5.6). Aggro two-drops play poorly in this slow format, and its 1R activation costs too much to use well. Even in R/W (−2.6) it's below replacement. Don't pick it.
Jiang Yanggu, Alone: Filler top-end (52.9%). A 5-mana 4/4 menace that loots and grows itself is fine, but cheap bodies without lasting impact fall off and R/W aggro is weak. Only marginal positives in R/W (+1.3) and B/R (+1.1). Late pick, 23rd card.
Kiora of Fire and Ashes: Premium uncommon, pick over most rares. 61.3% GIH and +8.2 IWD. Two must-answer threats for 6 mana, then a repeatable 8-mana dragon mode that wins stalled boards. It's +9 or more in B/G, R/G and U/R, and positive in every pair. LR's S grade (#875) supersedes the pre-data 3.0. Splash it if you have to.
Koth, the Geomancer: Trap: 51.6% with negative IWD in every pair, even B/R (−2.1), the home LoL picked for it. Heartwood ramp doesn't trigger landfall, and a 3/2 with occasional pings is just a weak three-drop in this format. LLU's C−/D+ was right; avoid it.
Marwyn, the Clearcutter: Playable 1-drop: 55.2%. Its 58.1% OH vs 53.1% GD says it's best early, and the sacrifice-for-cards mode gives it late value. It's mildly positive in every red pair (+1.6 in R/G with Heartwoods). It beats the LR read but isn't an early pick.
Pia, Determined Rebuilder: Solid playable. Two bodies for 3, including an evasive Thopter, play at 56.3%. The late-game pump gives it a mana sink for stalled boards. Positive in every red pair, best in U/R (+3.4) and R/G (+2.5), where artifacts and Heartwoods scale the pump. LR's B fits better than LLU's C+. Take it early in red.
Samut, Hazoret's Champion: Strong two-drop: 56.3% GIH, +3.1 IWD, positive in every red pair (R/G +3.2, R/W +3.1). High OH WR (58.5%) means it wins by punishing slow starts from landcycling opponents. Take it early for red aggro; it is weaker as a late topdeck.
Tetsuko Umezawa, Pursuer: Overrated. 52.2% fits the format's verdict that prowess underperforms; the double-striking 2/4 gets chumped or traded with in stalled boards. U/R is the only home (+2.0), and only with lots of cheap spells. Sideboard-tier everywhere else.
Tomik, Izzet Sparkmage: Trap outside a dedicated pinger deck: 51.3% and flat or negative everywhere (R/G -4.8). The 2-mana 1/2 prowess body is weak, and the damage boost needs many ping sources, which only near-mono-red reliably has (LLU). TCG's 4.0 was wrong. Take it late as a combo piece, never early.
Way of the Pyromancer: Trap; one of the weak Ways. 51.7%, negative in R/G (-1.1), R/W and B/R (-3.2), and only flat in U/R. The mana ability eats your one Jace activation per turn, and the ramp has few payoffs. LLU 259's data check beats TCG's 4.0. Use it only to fill a curve in R/G.
Way of the Warlord: Filler, not the removal LR graded B+. A -4 for 2 damage costs most of the token, and the data agrees: 53.3% overall, +2.9 only in UR, and negative in WR/RG/BR. LLU's Mark (D+) was closer. Take it for UR control and mid-pack at best elsewhere.
Winter, Team Player: Trap: 48.0% GIH and about -4 IWD in U/R, W/R and B/R alike. A 5-mana 3/3 that only grows your team when you cast spells loses badly in a format of stalled boards and sweepers, and convoke means tapping creatures you wanted to attack with. Don't play it.
Edgar, Moonlit Sovereign: Trap: 49.7% despite B grades, worst in R/G (−4.7). A five-mana 4/4 flash ambush loses to the format's bounce and removal, and it only grows if you skip casting spells. LLU's 'Unsummon target' read is correct. Take a landcycler instead.
Fblthp, Knows the Way: Premium green pick, closer to Mark's A− than Alex's B (57.7%, +4.6). It's a body plus 2–3 lands that fixes splashes and fuels card draw. Huge in G/U (+7.8) and G/W (+3.7). Add an off-colour basic even with no splash to raise its power.
Garruk, Curse Breaker: Bomb. Slam it. 65.5% GIH and +12.9 IWD: the -3 alone makes a 4/4 trampler, draws a card, and leaves a planeswalker on 2 loyalty. It's +12 to +15 in every green pair, peaking in W/G (+14.8) and B/G (+14.0). Numot's lukewarm 'seems good' is badly wrong. Take it over anything but the top mythics.
Ghalta the Unstoppable: Role-player at 53.2%, fitting LLU 259's 'play it, don't take it highly'. It realistically costs 4–5 once you have a 4/4 out. Best in G/U (+5.8) and B/G (+3.5), which have big bodies; nearly flat in R/G and G/W. Pick it mid-pack as a closer for big-green decks.
Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone: Solid playable: five stats across two bodies for 4 mana holds the ground well. 55.4% with +2.6 IWD, best in U/G (+4.8), where the untap also helps Heartwoods. LR's B+ overrates it; take it as a reliable mid-pack four-drop.
Loot, the Nexus: G/U-only ramp. It is +6.6 in G/U and about -0.7 in every other green pair. The fragile 2/1 dork pays off only when you have big draw spells and Jace-fed mana sinks to use the extra mana on. The 52.4% overall says LR's B was too high. Take it early only for G/U; otherwise it's filler.
Marwyn, the Preserver: Filler: 54.2% GIH, +0.1 IWD. A 3/2 for 2 whose land recursion matters only in long games. G/U (+3.4) is its only positive home; negative in R/G and G/W. Pick it mid-pack as a curve body, never a priority.
Pia, Aether Ascetic: Narrow build-around; 49.6% and a 22% play rate. It only works with several A-level enchantments (Plan for All Outcomes, the good Ways) and flashback discard fodder. Slight positive in G/U (+1.6), disastrous in R/G (-4.7). Leave it in most decks.
Ruric Thar, Magecrusher: Solid top end for ramp: 54.4%, but 56.6% when drawn vs 50.9% in the opening hand, typical of a 7-drop. Best in G/U (+4.4) and B/G (+3.6); only +1.4 in R/G, where Crusher and Kiora are better (LLU). It can be chump-blocked and loses to edicts, so play at most one.
Titanbones, Towering Heart: Filler-minus: 51.9%, negative even in its supposed G/W home (-0.3). G/W has too few repeatable lifegain sources to grow it, and 3 toughness dies to everything. LR's 'exactly what this format is not about' and LLU's D are right; TCG's lifegain 4.0 is wrong. A 23rd card at most.
Way of the Paradox: Solid Way, better than LR's C. Three mana for empower 5 plus a ramp land is efficient, and the lifegain adds up. 56.6% with +4.2 IWD, peaking in UG (+7.5) with real value in WG lifegain (+3.9, LLU 259). Early pick in UG, good in G/W.
Way of the Wildspeaker: Good playable that's at its best in G/U: 54.5% GIH overall, but +6.2 in G/U, where repeated empowers turn every Jace into another 4/4 trampler. Close to zero in other green pairs. 84% play rate, so experts put it in every green deck. Take it early for G/U, mid-pack otherwise.
Yoshimaru, Scrappy Stray: Playable green removal at 53.9%, below its 3.5 grade. Like other fight effects it needs a big creature already out, so it's weak early (50.7% opening hand). Good in G/U (+3.3) with Jace/Compel support; roughly flat in R/G, B/G and G/W. Count it as half a removal spell.
Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord: Filler two-drop at 52.9%; it adds nothing even in W/B (0.0 IWD). The 2/3 body holds the ground, but the sac outlet rarely has fodder below rare. LR's B−/B was optimistic; it isn't enough to pull you into W/B.
Hapatra, the Desert Fang: Premium removal-on-a-body. 59.2% GIH and +5.5 IWD. The MV-6 landcyclers and self-mill make its ETB kill almost anything. It's best in U/B (+6.3) and B/G (+5.2), where recurring it is the plan, and weak in B/R (+1.1). LR's B+/A- holds up. Take it early if you're black-green or black-blue.
Karn, Gilded Guardian: Filler: 52.7% with an 8.9% play rate. It plays as a 7-ish-mana 5/5 vigilance trample in R/G or B/G Heartwood decks that draws one or two cards. The pre-data Numot and LLU reads were right: only take it late as a top-end in token decks.
Kiora of Salt and Sand: Narrow U/G build-around. It's +4.5 in U/G, but 53.7% GIH and a 33.7% play rate mean it rarely makes decks, and the 8/8 almost never happens (per LR 876). A 3-mana 2/4 that guards Jace is fine. Take it late, and only in heavy-empower U/G.
Mabel, Valley Hero: Trap outside dedicated R/W go-wide. At 50.7% it is negative even in R/W (-1.4), and +1/+1 counters underperform in this slow, sweeper-heavy format. LR 874 marked it down ('really underperformed'), which overrides Alex's B-. Take it only if you are already deep in R/W with Warrior's Blades.
Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar: Strong gold uncommon: 56.8% GIH, +4.3 IWD. She plays best in spell-dense W/U (+6.0) and U/B (+4.7) decks that can protect her, as LoL's triple-Countersculpt deck did. Don't tap out for her on turn 4 into open removal; cast her on 6 with counter backup.
Tam, the Possibility: Unplayable, as the F and C- grades said; too few games for a WR, so this read is provisional. It's a vanilla 2/4 for 3 because no deck casts enough planeswalkers or reaches WUBRG. Don't be fooled by the rare.
Vraska, Soul of Stone: Narrow 3-colour build-around (53.4%). The +3.9 IWD in U/R shows it works in a spell-heavy deck, but two colours plus a splash beats three, and its 41% play rate shows how often it's left out. It's worse than Saheeli (LR). Play it only if you're U/R with white mana already; LLU's D+ is right for everyone else.
Vraska, the Cutting Glare: Bomb-tier: 62.4%, +8.9 IWD. A 3-mana 4/4 deathtouch is a strong blocker early. With six lands it's a Chupacabra on any permanent late, and recursion loops it. Best in U/B (+11.6) and B/G (+8.5). Pick it over everything except true bombs. It's A-, matching LR and LLU.
Karn, Argent Defender: Sideboard only. A 1/3 that stops ETB triggers, including your own Keeper and creature empowers; 50.0% with a 9% play rate. Bring it in Bo3 against ETB-heavy decks when your own deck doesn't rely on ETBs. Never maindeck it.
Traxos, Scourge Eternal: Trap: 51.5% GIH and -4.7 in R/G, the ramp deck that should want it most. A 5/4 trampler that enters with no effect and only untaps when you cast creatures gets blocked or removed in a slow format. Alex's C− beats LR's B; play it only if you're short on four-drops.
Eye of Ugin: Provisional read with no win-rate data and a 0.6% play rate: it's an Eldrazi tutor land in a set with almost no Eldrazi, so it does nothing. LR grades it F. Don't play it; take it only for collection value.
Austere Command: Bomb: take it and splash it (61.7%, +7.9 IWD, ALSA 2.0). In a stall-heavy format a modal, often one-sided wrath is a game-winner; pick the creature mode your board survives. LR 874 named it LSV's example of a splash-worthy bomb. No per-pair data; it's playable in any white deck.
Flesh Duplicate: Solid playable. 55.7% GIH, but +4.6 IWD says it improves the decks it's in more than the WR suggests. LR reads it as a 2-mana clone with vanishing 3: copy their best ETB creature, attack twice, and it's gone. It has no grade and only one expert note, so it gets a moderately early pick in blue.
Consign to Memory: Provisional read (no WR data; 2.5% play rate): sideboard at best, per LR's F. Its narrow counter has almost nothing to hit in Limited, so don't main-deck it.
Sublime Epiphany: Bomb: 66.9% with +14.5 IWD, among the best cards in the set. Six mana at instant speed counters, bounces, copies and draws, a massive multi-for-one in a slow format where opponents won't play around it. Slam it in any blue deck and consider splashing it.
Consider: Solid blue playable that goes mid-pack (ALSA 5.0). At 56.5% the 1-mana surveil cantrip feeds W/U surveil payoffs and U/B threshold and smooths draws in a format where running out of action loses. The 58.5% GD makes it more than a free roll, and LR's C+ undersold it. Pair data is pending, so this read is partly provisional.
Necrodominance: Provisional: no live data, no card text in the feed, 10.9% play rate, only a garbled LR note that seems to say play it. As a bonus-sheet black mythic card-draw engine, play it in grindy U/B or B/G control and avoid it in aggro.
Mind Twist: Bomb: 64.6% GIH and +12.5 IWD, among the set's best. In a slow, card-advantage format, X=3-4 on turn 5-6 empties their hand and they can't recover. Slam it in any black deck and splash it if you can; LR's B+ undersold it.
Splinter Twin: Provisional read (thin record, no card text): 62.8% with +10.9 IWD is strong, but probably inflated because it's mostly played when the Divining Duelist infinite-copy combo is assembled. LR rates it F outside the combo. Take it if you have Duelist or can pick one up cheaply; otherwise rate it a playable aura at best.
Root Maze: Don't take it (provisional, no live WR, 0.8% play rate). The bonus-sheet tapping symmetric enchantment does nothing for a Limited deck and slows your own landcyclers and duals. LR's F is the only grade, and it's correct.
